messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Alert: high paging and model-warmup failures on us-west-2-prod. 90% of load-warmup jobs failing with OOM/deser errors, node flaps observed. Affects model: gptx-6b-quant-v2. Investigate and coordinate handoff. #severity:sev2

alice_oncall: I'm on it. Confirming scope — which pools?

ben_runtime: us-west-2 cluster: inference-pool-3 primarily. Warmup attempts spike when autoscaler provisions new nodes. Seeing repeated: "CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS" and "OOM when allocating tensor" in model init.

carmen_sre: we've got a node that rebooted twice in last 5m. Kernel logs show GPU driver reset. Paging I/O is high on the attached NVMe. Could be artifact cache eviction thrash.

dave_ml: quick hypothesis: the quantized artifact has a corrupted shard causing large temporary allocations during deserializing. Compile times also jump to >45s which times out warmup path.

alice_oncall: mitigation idea: stop warmup autoscale for that model, route new requests to gptx-6b-quant-v1 fallback variant, and spin up a smaller warmup instance with reduced batch_size=1. Can someone patch routing?

ben_runtime: I can push an emergency route change: set policy for model alias gptx-6b -> gptx-6b-quant-v1 for dedicated tier. Applying now.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: route-update triggered by ben_runtime at 1732109950 — gptx-6b alias now points to gptx-6b-quant-v1 for traffic tier=standard.

elaine_support: heads-up — CS/Support: customers using model alias "gptx-6b" may see degraded throughput but service should remain up on fallback. Drafting banner.

frank_cs: Please include expected ETA for restore and whether we expect data/response format changes. Customers asking.

alice_oncall: ETA for rollback ~30-45m depending on artifact fix. No response format changes — variants are functionally compatible. I'll confirm after we stabilize.

carmen_sre: meanwhile I'm isolating the problematic nodes and cordoning them: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-uw2-12` then draining pods to avoid further hardware resets.

ben_runtime: draining done. Also disabled warmup concurrency for pool= inference-pool-3: `PATCH /config/warmup?pool=inference-pool-3&concurrency=0` — reduces simultaneous warmup jobs.

dave_ml: I pulled the artifact shard logs. There's a stack trace during deserialization: \n```\nDeserializeShard failed: unexpected EOF\nAllocating temp buffer 1.9GB\nCUDA error: illegal memory access\n```\nLooks like truncated shard triggered large buffer allocation then GPU crash.

alice_oncall: Can we replace the artifact with a verified copy from s3? dave_ml, do you have a clean checksum?

dave_ml: yes — pulling s3://redwood-models/gptx-6b-quant-v2/checksums.txt and verifying. Two shards fail checksum. I'll trigger re-upload of those shards and update artifact manifest.

incident-bot: storage-bot: started artifact-replace job at 1732110120 for gptx-6b-quant-v2 shards [0371, 0440].

carmen_sre: After cordon+drain we still saw one node flap while image-puller retried. I've increased kubelet image-pull backoff and turned on swapless mount to reduce disk pressure.

ben_runtime: After routing to fallback, 95% user requests are successful. Error rate on primary variant down from 18% -> 2%. CPU/GPU utilization normalizing.

elaine_support: Banner posted to status.redwood.com: "Investigating model warmup failures in us-west-2; fallback models in use; some customers may see higher latency." I included CI ticket link.

frank_cs: Got customer note: "We're OK with slower responses but need SLA confirmation." I'm collecting affected org IDs for incident timeline.

alice_oncall: Good. Next steps: (1) finish artifact swap and integrity check (dave), (2) slowly re-enable warmup with rate-limit and smaller concurrency (ben), (3) monitor paging and GPU errors (carmen). If stable after 30m, revert alias.

dave_ml: artifact-replace finished at 1732110320. Manifest updated and new checksums match. I'm kicking a controlled warmup on a single node: `./tooling/warmup --model gptx-6b-quant-v2 --nodes 1 --batch 1`

carmen_sre: watching kernel logs + nvidia-smi on warmup node. No driver resets so far. Paging I/O low.

ben_runtime: re-enabled warmup concurrency=1 for pool inference-pool-3 and set a compile-timeout bump to 80s to avoid timeouts for first build.

incident-bot: monitoring-bot: thermal spike metrics and paging errors trending down. Error rate on v2 warmup attempts: 0/12 failures in last 10m.

alice_oncall: Nice. Starting gradual traffic shift back to v2: 10% -> 30% -> 60% checks for 5m windows. Ben, trigger traffic shift when ready.

ben_runtime: shifting to 10% now.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: alias traffic: 10%->v2 at 1732110420.

carmen_sre: Observability good at 10%. No flaps. GPU memory stable.

ben_runtime: shifting to 30%.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: alias traffic: 30%->v2 at 1732110440.

elaine_support: Updated customers: fallback removed for some orgs moved back to v2 at 30% — messaging updated.

frank_cs: Customer reply: "Thanks for quick mitigation, will keep monitoring on our side."

alice_oncall: After 30m of stable behavior we'll close the active alert and file a postmortem. Carmen, please capture kernel logs & node timeline. Ben and Dave, include artifact pre/post checksums and warmup timing. Elaine/Frank, include customer impact summary.

carmen_sre: collecting logs now, exporting to /incidents/1732109876/archives.

ben_runtime: I'll open a follow-up RFC to add artifact checksum validation in the warmup path to fail fast instead of allocating huge buffers.

dave_ml: also propose adding shard-level deserialization sanity checks and smaller temp buffer allocation thresholds.

alice_oncall: Great. Closing active mitigation phase — keeping the thread open for postmortem notes. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
